chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Singer Arthur Lee Simpkins joins the Chicago band at Swingland
summary: Corrects dates: New York was the late twenties, Chicago the thirties. Georgia Boy Arthur Lee Simpkins became an opera-style tenor in Europe and was hired at Swingland after singing with Earl Hines.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We are going to review some of those dates. You were talking about the late thirties, and I think you meant really the twenties, right?
I had New York and Chicago mixed. New York was the late twenties. Chicago was the thirties.
One thing that you had mentioned earlier, that you said you'd refer back to, was the vocalist that you had with your band, Arthur Lee Simpkins.

Yes. Now Arthur Lee Simpkins was with the Chicago band. We called him Georgia Boy. He was actually from Georgia. This guy was internationally known because he later become a great -- what do you call it? -- a lyric tenor? And he toured Europe. He sang in different languages. Oh, six or seven different languages. He was --
Was he singing opera, you mean, or --
Opera. Yes. In fact, my wife just brought in a picture here. Let him see this, Angel, maybe you're familiar with -- the guy on the extreme end on the left, Arthur Lee Simpkins.

He is well known in California, in fact, all over. Incidentally, he just passed here recently, I found out from Billy Daniels who was here in Denver at the Warehouse, a few weeks ago. He came by to see me where I was playing at the (unintelligible), and Billy Daniels told me that Arthur Lee Simpkins had passed. And the last time I saw Arthur Lee when he was alive was in Los Angeles. He had a string of apartment buildings about a block long. (Inaudible). And he always toured Europe. And the guy was -- he was getting seven thousand a week. So you know he was one of the top guys.
And he made quite a few records -- spiritual things, and -- but he was my vocalist.
I see. Now was he your vocalist at Wilberforce?

I met him in Chicago at Swingland -- a place called Swingland that I used to broadcast from there, with this particular big band, and he came in one day and he knew the owner, and the owner told me, he said, 'Here's a guy you ought to get for your vocalist. He's a great singer.' So I had him sing a couple of numbers with the band, and that was it.

He had been down originally and sang with Earl Hines. He was at the Grand Terrace. But he liked our group better, cause I don't why. But he joined us, and we were together for, oh, three or four years. He was our vocalist, and we used to broadcast from WBBM in Chicago. A great band. In fact, speaking of -- can we talk a little about Chicago?
